summaryEn: From Starbase, ahead of a Starship flight test, Elon Musk delivers SpaceX's Starship and Mars update — unveiling the Starship V3 design and the plan to make life multiplanetary.
summaryZh: 在星舰飞行测试前夕，埃隆·马斯克在星基地介绍了SpaceX星舰和火星计划的最新进展——揭晓星舰V3设计，以及让生命成为多行星物种的计划。

segments.textEn: Yeah, there you go.
segments.textZh: 对，就是这样。

segments.textEn: All right. The gateway to Mars.
segments.textZh: 好。通往火星的门户。

segments.textEn: So here we are, here we are at the newly incorporated Starbase Texas.
segments.textZh: 所以，我们现在就在这里，我们现在位于新近建市的得克萨斯州星基地。

segments.textEn: This is the first new city made in America in, I think, quite a few decades, that, at least that's what I'm told. And very cool name. And it's named that because it is where we're going to develop the technology necessary to take humanity and civilization and life as we know it to another planet for the first time in the four and a half billion year history of Earth.
segments.textZh: 我想，这是美国几十年来建立的第一座新城市，至少别人是这么告诉我的。而且名字非常酷。之所以这样命名，是因为我们将在这里开发必要的技术，在地球45亿年的历史上首次把人类、文明和我们所知的生命带到另一个星球。

segments.textEn: So go with this little video here. This is how it started off, with basically nothing. So they started off as basically a sandbar with nothing.
segments.textZh: 来看一下这里的这段小视频。这就是它起步时的样子，基本上什么都没有。所以，他们起步的地方基本上就是一片什么都没有的沙洲。

segments.textEn: Even those little things we built, obviously.
segments.textZh: 显然，就连那些小东西也是我们建的。

segments.textEn: That's the original sort of Mad Max rocket.
segments.textZh: 那就是最初那种《疯狂的麦克斯》式火箭。

segments.textEn: This is where you discover light lighting is very important for that Mad Max rocket.
segments.textZh: 就是在这里，你发现灯光照明对那枚《疯狂的麦克斯》式火箭非常重要。

segments.textEn: So, yeah, not that ago there was basically nothing here. And in the space of about five or six years, thanks to the incredible work of the SpaceX team, we've built a small city and we've built two gigantic launch pads and a gigantic rocket factory for a gigantic rocket. So, and the cool thing is, for anyone out there who's watching this, you can actually come and visit because our entire production facility and launch site are on a public highway.
segments.textZh: 所以，是的，就在不久以前，这里还基本上什么都没有。在大约5或6年的时间里，得益于SpaceX团队令人难以置信的工作，我们建起了一座小城市、2座巨型发射台，以及一座为巨型火箭服务的巨型火箭工厂。所以，而且很酷的一点是，对于正在观看这段视频的任何人来说，你实际上可以来参观，因为我们的整个生产设施和发射场都位于一条公共公路旁。

segments.textEn: So anyone comes who comes to South Texas can come and see the rocket pretty close up and see the factory. And so anyone who's interested in seeing the largest flying object on Earth can come here anytime they want and just drive down the public highway and see it, which is pretty cool. So then we progress to where we are now, StarVase 2025.
segments.textZh: 所以，任何来的人，任何来到南得克萨斯州的人，都可以相当近距离地看火箭，也可以看工厂。因此，任何有兴趣观看地球上最大飞行物体的人，都可以随时来这里，只需沿着公共公路开车过来就能看到它，这非常酷。然后我们逐步发展到了如今的样子，StarVase 2025。

segments.textEn: So we're now at the point where we can produce a ship roughly every two or three weeks.
segments.textZh: 所以，我们现在已经到了大约每2或3周能生产1艘飞船的阶段。

segments.textEn: Now, we don't always produce the ship every two or three weeks because we are making design upgrades. But ultimately we're aiming the ability to produce a thousand ships a year, so three ships a day.
segments.textZh: 现在，我们并不总是每2或3周生产1艘飞船，因为我们正在进行设计升级。但最终，我们的目标是具备每年生产1000艘飞船的能力，也就是每天3艘。

segments.textEn: So that's where things are now. I'm standing in that building, That's our hovercraft.
segments.textZh: 所以，这就是目前的情况。我正站在那座建筑里，那是我们的气垫船。

segments.textEn: We're driving a booster down the road to the launch site.
segments.textZh: 我们正把一枚助推器沿公路运往发射场。

segments.textEn: You can see the mega bays.
segments.textZh: 你们可以看到那些超级厂房。

segments.textEn: And as I said, what's cool, the cool thing for those out there watching this video is that you can actually just literally come here, drive down the road and see it, which is the first time in history that that's been possible. So all this cool stuff you that, that that road on the left there, that highway is public and you can just come here and see it, which I recommend doing. I think it's very inspiring to See, so that's our gigabay.
segments.textZh: 正如我所说，很酷的是，对于正在观看这段视频的各位来说，你们真的可以直接来这里，沿着这条路开车就能看到它，这是历史上第一次有这种可能。所以所有这些很酷的东西，你们，那条，那那边左侧的道路，那条公路是公共公路，你们可以直接来这里观看，我建议大家这么做。我认为亲眼看到这一切非常鼓舞人心，所以那就是我们的超级厂房。

segments.textEn: So where we're expanding integration to produce a thousand starships per year.
segments.textZh: 所以，我们正在扩大总装能力，以便每年生产1000艘星舰。

segments.textEn: Well yeah, that hasn't been built yet, but we're building it.
segments.textZh: 嗯，是的，那还没有建成，但我们正在建。

segments.textEn: That is a truly enormous structure. This will be one that'll be one of the biggest structures, I think by some measures the biggest structure in the world.
segments.textZh: 那是一座真正庞大的建筑。我想，它将会是最大的建筑之一，按某些衡量标准，它会是世界上最大的建筑。

segments.textEn: And it's designed for a thousand starships a year.
segments.textZh: 它是按照每年生产1000艘星舰设计的。

segments.textEn: We're also building a gigabay in Florida bringing, so we'll have two facilities, one in Texas and one in Florida.
segments.textZh: 我们还在佛罗里达州建造一座超级厂房，这样，我们就会有2处设施，1处在得克萨斯州，1处在佛罗里达州。

segments.textEn: It's actually difficult to gauge the size of these buildings because you need a kind of human for scale. When you see how tiny a human is next to that building, you realize just how enormous it is.
segments.textZh: 实际上很难判断这些建筑有多大，因为你需要用一个人之类的东西作为比例参照。当你看到一个人在那座建筑旁边显得多么渺小时，就会意识到它究竟有多么庞大。

segments.textEn: So when we look at our build comparison vehicles per year, and so you look at Boeing and Airbus making airplanes, Starship will be making at some point probably as many starships for Mars as Boeing and Airbus make commercial airplanes. So this is really at a scale, enormous scale. And each starship will have a capability.
segments.textZh: 所以，当我们对比每年制造的飞行器数量时，你们可以看看波音和空客制造的飞机，星舰在某个时候为火星制造的星舰数量，很可能会与波音和空客制造的商用飞机一样多。所以，这确实达到了规模，非常庞大的规模。而且每艘星舰都将具备一种能力。

segments.textEn: Each starship is bigger than a 747 or an A380. Like it's truly enormous.
segments.textZh: 每艘星舰都比747或A380更大。它确实非常庞大。

segments.textEn: And then in terms of Starship Starlink satellites, the version three satellites making on the order of 5,000 a year, maybe at some point closer to 10,000 a year. And those sonic V3 satellites are each the size of roughly a 737. They're pretty big.
segments.textZh: 然后就星舰星链卫星而言，第三版卫星的年产量约为5000颗，也许在某个时候会接近每年10000颗。而那些音速V3卫星，每颗的尺寸大约相当于1架737。它们相当大。

segments.textEn: That compares to the B24 bomber in World War II.
segments.textZh: 这可以与第二次世界大战中的B24轰炸机相比。

segments.textEn: Now it's still small compared to Tesla.
segments.textZh: 不过，与Tesla相比，这仍然很小。

segments.textEn: So and Tesla will probably doing, you know, double or triple that volume in the future. So it just puts things into perspective that it is actually possible to build a vast number of interplanetary starships. And even when you can compare things on the tonnage standpoint, Tesla and other car companies still building far more complex manufactured tonnage than than SpaceX. Which is really a way of saying that it's very achievable.
segments.textZh: 所以，Tesla未来的产量很可能会达到那个数字的2倍或3倍。这样就能让事情有个参照：建造数量庞大的星际星舰实际上是可能的。即使从吨位角度进行比较，Tesla和其他汽车公司所制造的复杂产品吨位仍然远远超过SpaceX。这其实就是说，这完全可以实现。

segments.textEn: Like these numbers, while they are insanely high by traditional space standards, are achievable by humans because they have been achieved in other industries. Progress is measured by the timeline to establishing a self sustaining civilization on Mars. That's how we're gauging our progress here at Starbase. So with each launch, especially in the early days of Starship, each launch is about learning more and more about what's needed to make life multi planetary and to improve starship to the point where it can be taking ultimately hundreds of thousands, if not millions of people to Mars.
segments.textZh: 这些数字虽然按照传统航天标准高得惊人，但人类有能力实现，因为其他行业已经实现过这样的数字。进展以在火星上建立自给自足文明的时间表来衡量。这就是我们在星基地衡量进展的方式。因此，随着每一次发射，尤其是在星舰发展的早期阶段，每次发射都是为了越来越深入地了解，要让生命实现多行星化需要什么，并不断改进星舰，直到它最终能够把数十万人、乃至数百万人送往火星。

segments.textEn: Ideally we can take anyone who wants to go to Mars? We can take to Mars and bring with it, bring all of the equipment necessary to make Mars self sustaining so Mars can grow by itself in a worst case scenario. Getting to the point where the fundamental fork in the road for human destiny is where Mars can continue to grow even if the supply ships from Earth stop coming for any reason. At that point we've achieved civilizational resilience where Mars can potentially come to the rescue of Earth if something goes wrong.
segments.textZh: 理想情况下，我们可以把任何想去火星的人带去火星？我们可以把他们带到火星，并随之带去、带去让火星实现自给自足所必需的全部设备，这样在最坏的情况下，火星也能自行发展。关键是要走到人类命运的根本岔路口，也就是即便来自地球的补给飞船因任何原因停止抵达，火星仍能继续发展。到那时，我们就实现了文明韧性；如果地球出了什么问题，火星或许能前来拯救地球。

segments.textEn: Or maybe Earth could come to the rescue of Mars, but, well, but having two planets that are, that are, that can, that, that are both self sustaining and strong I think is going to be incredibly important for the long term survival of civilization.
segments.textZh: 或者也许地球可以前来拯救火星，但是，嗯，但是拥有2颗都、都、能够、都、都能自给自足且强大的行星，我认为这对文明的长期生存会极其重要。

segments.textEn: So like just, I think any given civilization is likely to last maybe, I don't know, 10 times longer, maybe much longer if it is a multi planet civilization than if it is a single planet civilization. Because there's always some chance that, you know, us humans could do something crazy like World War Three. Hopefully not, but it's possible. Or that there could be some natural event like meteors or super volcanoes or something that we don't expect.
segments.textZh: 所以，就是，我认为任何一个文明，如果是多行星文明，而不是单行星文明，都可能延续得，也许，我不知道，长10倍，也许还要长得多。因为总有某种可能，你知道，我们人类可能会做出一些疯狂的事，比如第三次世界大战。希望不会，但这是有可能的。或者可能发生某种自然事件，比如流星、超级火山，或某种我们意料之外的事情。

segments.textEn: And then if you only have one planet, then that could be curtains. But if we got two planets, we keep going and then we go beyond Mars ultimately to maybe the asteroid belt, the moons of Jupiter and beyond, and ultimately to other star systems and we can be out there among the stars making science fiction no longer fiction. So in order to achieve this goal, we have to be, we have to make rapidly reusable rockets so that the, the cost per flight, the cost per ton to Mars is as low as possible.
segments.textZh: 那么，如果你只有1颗行星，那可能就完了。但如果我们有2颗行星，我们就能继续前进，然后最终越过火星，或许前往小行星带、木星的卫星以及更远的地方，并最终前往其他恒星系；我们可以置身群星之间，让科幻不再是虚构。所以，为了实现这个目标，我们必须，我们必须制造可快速重复使用的火箭，从而让，让每次飞行的成本、运往火星的每吨成本尽可能低。

segments.textEn: That's essential. So for that rapidly reusable rockets, I said it's actually four hours or it's like a pirate, it's like rapidly reusable. Reliable rockets is the key. Rrrr.
segments.textZh: 这是必不可少的。所以，对于可快速重复使用的火箭，我说其实是4小时，或者它就像个海盗，就像是快速重复使用。可靠的火箭才是关键。Rrrr。

segments.textEn: Now we've congrats the SpaceX team on making incredible progress on catching a giant rocket.
segments.textZh: 现在，我们已经祝贺了SpaceX团队在接住一枚巨型火箭方面取得的惊人进展。

segments.textEn: So it's really mind blowing that the SpaceX team has been able to catch the largest flying object ever made multiple times using a very novel method of catching it out of the air with giant chopsticks.
segments.textZh: 所以，SpaceX团队能够多次使用一种非常新颖的方法，用巨型筷子从空中接住有史以来最大的飞行物体，这真的令人震撼。

segments.textEn: I mean, have you ever seen that before?
segments.textZh: 我是说，你们以前见过那样的情景吗？

segments.textEn: Yeah, congrats again. That was an incredible achievement.
segments.textZh: 是的，再次表示祝贺。那是一项令人难以置信的成就。

segments.textEn: So the reason we are catching it in this way, which has never been done before, is in order to achieve the rapidly reusable portion of the, in order to make the rocket rapidly reusable. So if it is, if the super heavy booster, which is gigantic, it's like 30ft in diameter.
segments.textZh: 所以，我们用这种前所未有的方式接住它，是为了实现其中可快速重复使用的部分，为了让火箭能够快速重复使用。所以，如果它，如果这个巨大的超重型助推器，它的直径大约是30英尺。

segments.textEn: If it were to land with landing legs on a landing pad, we would then have to pick it up, stow the legs and put it back in the launch pad. And that's, it's quite difficult to transport such a large thing. But if we catch it with the same tower that it's used to put it in the launch mount to begin with, that is the best case outcome for rapid reuse. So it literally gets caught by the same arms that placed it in the launch in launch ring and then it is placed back in the launch ring immediately.
segments.textZh: 如果它用着陆支腿降落在着陆台上，我们随后就必须把它吊起来，收起支腿，再把它放回发射台。而且，运输这么巨大的东西相当困难。但如果我们用一开始就用来把它放入发射支架的同一座塔架接住它，那就是实现快速重复使用的最佳结果。所以，它实际上会被当初将它放入发射、发射环的同一组机械臂接住，然后立刻被放回发射环。

segments.textEn: So in principle, the super heavy booster can be reflown within an hour of landing. So it comes back in about five or six minutes one way or another. And, and then it gets caught by the tower arms placed back in the launch mount. And then you can refill propellant in about 30 to 40 minutes and, and place a ship on top of it. And in principle refly the entire booster every hour, maybe every two hours to be, give it a little bit of extra time.
segments.textZh: 所以原则上，超重型助推器可以在着陆后1小时内再次飞行。所以无论如何，它大约5或6分钟后就会返回。而且，而且随后会被塔架机械臂接住，放回发射支架。然后，你可以在大约30至40分钟内重新加注推进剂，并且，并且在它上面放置一艘飞船。原则上，整个助推器可以每小时再次飞行一次，也许每2小时一次，这样，可以给它多一点额外时间。

segments.textEn: But let's just say it's, it's very, it's in the limit of rapid reuse.
segments.textZh: 但我们就说，它，它非常，它已经处在快速重复使用的极限上了。

segments.textEn: And then we, the next thing we need to do is catch the ship too.
segments.textZh: 然后，我们接下来还需要做的是也把飞船接住。

segments.textEn: So we haven't done this yet, but we will.
segments.textZh: 所以我们还没有做到这一点，但我们会做到。

segments.textEn: So that's what we hope to demonstrate later this year, maybe as soon as two or three months from now.
segments.textZh: 所以这就是我们希望在今年晚些时候演示的内容，也许最快在2或3个月后。

segments.textEn: And then the ship would be placed on top of the booster and then again refilled with repellent and flown again with the ship. It takes a bit longer because it's got to orbit Earth a few times until the ground track comes back over the launch pad. But the ship is also intended to be reflown multiple times per day.
segments.textZh: 然后飞船会被放到助推器顶部，接着再次加满驱避剂，并与飞船一起再次飞行。这需要更长一点时间，因为它必须绕地球飞行几圈，直到地面轨迹再次经过发射台上空。但飞船的设计目标也是每天重复飞行多次。

segments.textEn: This is the, the new Raptor 3, which is an awesome engine. Big hand to the Raptor team for this. This is very exciting.
segments.textZh: 这是，这台新的Raptor 3，它是一台非常出色的发动机。请为Raptor团队热烈鼓掌。这非常令人兴奋。

segments.textEn: So Raptor 3 is designed to require no basic heat shield, saving a lot of mass on the bottom and actually improving reliability. So that if, if there is for example, small fuel leak from the Raptor engine, it will simply leak into the existing flaming plasma and not really matter. Whereas a fuel leak when the engines are contained in a box is a very scary thing indeed. So this is a Raptor 3. It'll take it probably a few kicks at the can, but it will be is a massive increase in payload capability, in engine efficiency and in reliability.
segments.textZh: 所以Raptor 3的设计不需要基本隔热罩，从而节省底部的大量质量，并且实际上提高了可靠性。这样一来，如果，如果出现例如Raptor发动机少量燃料泄漏的情况，它只会泄漏到现有的炽热等离子体中，实际上不会有什么影响。而当发动机被封闭在一个箱体中时，燃料泄漏确实是一件非常可怕的事。所以这是一台Raptor 3。它可能还需要尝试几次，但它将会是、是有效载荷能力、发动机效率和可靠性的一次巨大提升。

segments.textEn: So this is really a revolutionary engine. Raptor 3 is really, I'd say, kind of alien technology rocket engine.
segments.textZh: 所以这确实是一台革命性的发动机。Raptor 3确实，我会说，有点像外星科技火箭发动机。

segments.textEn: I mean even industry experts, when we showed a picture of the Raptor 3 said that engine is not complete. So then we said well here's the engine not complete. Firing at a level of efficiency that has never been achieved before.
segments.textZh: 我是说，就连行业专家在我们展示Raptor 3的照片时都说，那台发动机还没有完成。于是我们就说，好吧，这就是还没有完成的发动机。正以一种前所未有的效率水平点火运行。

segments.textEn: So.
segments.textZh: 所以。

segments.textEn: I mean that is one clean engine.
segments.textZh: 我是说，那真是一台干净利落的发动机。

segments.textEn: So in order to make the engine like that, we had to simplify. So many parts of the design incorporate secondary fluid circuits and electronics in the structure of the engine itself. So everything is contained and protected. It is a marvel of engineering, frankly.
segments.textZh: 所以，为了把发动机做成那样，我们必须简化。设计中的许多部件都把次级流体回路和电子设备整合进发动机本身的结构中。因此，一切都被容纳并保护起来。坦率地说，这是一个工程奇迹。

segments.textEn: Then one of the other technologies that's key for Mars is doing orbital propellant transfer. So you can think of this like similar to aerial refueling for airplanes, but in this case it's orbital refilling of rockets, which has never been done before. But it is, you know, technically feasible.
segments.textZh: 然后，对火星而言另一项关键技术是在轨推进剂转移。你可以把它想成类似飞机的空中加油，但在这里是在轨为火箭补充推进剂，这是以前从未实现过的。但它，你知道，在技术上是可行的。

segments.textEn: Always feel like these things are a little NSFW sort of listen, you got to transfer fluid somehow. There's no, this has got to be done.
segments.textZh: 总觉得这些东西有点不宜在工作场合观看，听着，你总得用某种方式转移流体。没办法，这件事必须完成。

segments.textEn: So the two starships would get together and one starship would transfer fuel and oxygen. And actually most of the mass is oxygen. It's almost 80% oxygen that gets transferred a little over 20% fuel.
